config.title: Write a deep clone utility without libraries

intro.title: Write a deep clone utility without libraries
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a utility function that creates a deep clone of a JavaScript object. A deep clone is a completely independent copy where nested objects and arrays are also duplicated, not just referenced. You will learn to handle different data types like objects, arrays, and primitives using recursion and type checking. This exercise will strengthen your understanding of object manipulation, recursion, and the structured clone algorithm's limitations in pure JavaScript.
intro.usecase: Deep cloning is essential when working with complex state management in interactive applications like dashboards or form builders. For example, when a user creates a duplicate dashboard panel with customized widgets, you need to copy all nested configuration objects without affecting the original. Similarly, in form builders where users can duplicate sections with nested field validations and conditional logic, deep cloning ensures independent copies. This pattern prevents subtle bugs where modifying a copied object accidentally changes the original data structure.

objectives: Implement a function that creates a deep copy of primitive values
Construct logic to handle different data types during cloning
Apply recursion to clone nested objects and arrays
Initialize a new object or array structure for each cloned level
Manipulate object properties to populate cloned structures
Control circular reference detection to prevent infinite recursion
Integrate type checking to determine appropriate cloning strategy

steps.title: Create the deepClone function signature
steps.instruction: Declare a function named deepClone that takes one parameter called obj.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. The function should accept a single parameter named obj.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named deepClone with one parameter obj is declared.
successCriteria: The code contains a function named deepClone that accepts one parameter named obj.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is named exactly 'deepClone' and accepts one parameter named 'obj'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function declaration is missing or incorrect. Please declare a function named deepClone that takes one parameter called obj.

steps.title: Handle primitive values and null
steps.instruction: Inside your deepClone function, add a check at the beginning to return the obj parameter immediately if it's null, not an object, or a primitive value.
steps.hint: You can check if obj is null or if typeof obj is not 'object' and return obj directly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The deepClone function will now handle primitive values, null, and non-object types by returning them unchanged.
successCriteria: The deepClone function has an early return statement that checks if obj is null or typeof obj is not 'object' and returns obj.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your check covers both null values and primitive types (like numbers, strings, booleans).
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't yet have the proper early return check. Remember to check if obj is null or if typeof obj is not 'object'.

steps.title: Handle Array objects
steps.instruction: Add an if statement to check if the input is an Array, and if so, create an empty array to hold the cloned elements.
steps.hint: You can use Array.isArray(obj) to detect arrays. Inside the if block, create a new array variable to store the cloned items.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will now detect arrays and prepare an empty array for cloning their elements.
successCriteria: The code includes an if statement using Array.isArray(obj) and creates an empty array variable inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you used Array.isArray(obj) and created an empty array inside the if block.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the hint: you need to detect arrays with Array.isArray(obj) and create an empty array to hold the cloned elements.

steps.title: Initialize the result variable
steps.instruction: Inside your deepClone function, declare a variable named 'result' and assign it an empty array if the input is an array, otherwise assign it an empty object.
steps.hint: You can use Array.isArray() to check if the input is an array. Use conditional assignment with the ternary operator or an if statement.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: variable initialization based on type
let container = Array.isArray(input) ? [] : {};
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a 'result' variable that is either an empty array or empty object, ready to be populated with cloned values.
successCriteria: A variable named 'result' is declared and assigned either [] or {} based on whether the input is an array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've declared the variable, but check if you're correctly determining whether the input is an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The result variable initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to check if the input is an array.

steps.title: Iterate through object properties
steps.instruction: Inside your deepClone function, add a for...in loop to iterate through all enumerable properties of the input object.
steps.hint: Use for...in syntax: for (let key in obj) { ... } to loop through each property name in the object.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your function should now include a for...in loop that will iterate through all properties of the input object when it's a regular object.
successCriteria: The deepClone function contains a for...in loop that iterates through the object's properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a proper for...in loop. Check that you're using the correct syntax: for (let key in obj) { ... }.
steps.feedbackWrong: The for...in loop is missing or incorrect. Remember to use for...in syntax to iterate through all enumerable properties of the object.

steps.title: Check property ownership
steps.instruction: Inside the for...in loop, add a check using hasOwnProperty to ensure you only process the object's own properties (not inherited ones).
steps.hint: Use an if statement with obj.hasOwnProperty(key) to verify the property belongs directly to the object before processing it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The for...in loop should include an if statement that checks if the property belongs directly to the object using hasOwnProperty.
successCriteria: The hasOwnProperty check is implemented inside the for...in loop to filter out inherited properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the for...in loop, but the hasOwnProperty check is missing or incomplete. Make sure to use obj.hasOwnProperty(key) inside an if statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hasOwnProperty check is not implemented correctly. Inside the for...in loop, add an if statement that checks if obj.hasOwnProperty(key) before processing the property.

steps.title: Add recursive call for nested objects
steps.instruction: Inside the for...in loop, after the hasOwnProperty check, assign to result[key] by recursively calling deepClone on obj[key].
steps.hint: Use the deepClone function itself to clone nested objects or arrays. This is the recursive step that makes the clone deep.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will now recursively clone nested objects and arrays when iterating through properties.
successCriteria: Inside the for...in loop, after the hasOwnProperty check, there is an assignment that calls deepClone(obj[key]) and assigns it to result[key].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling deepClone on obj[key] and assigning the result to result[key] inside the loop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The recursive call is missing or incorrect. Inside the loop, after checking hasOwnProperty, you need to assign result[key] = deepClone(obj[key]).

steps.title: Return the cloned result
steps.instruction: Add a return statement at the end of your deepClone function to return the cloned result variable.
steps.hint: After your for...in loop finishes, use 'return result;' to output the cloned object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The deepClone function will have a return statement that outputs the cloned object after all properties have been processed.
successCriteria: The function ends with 'return result;' (or equivalent) to return the cloned object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning the 'result' variable (or whatever you named your cloned object).
steps.feedbackWrong: The function needs a return statement at the end. After the loop finishes, add 'return result;' to output the cloned object.

steps.instruction: Create a test object with nested structures, arrays, dates, and primitive values to test your deepClone function. Add this object after your function definition.
steps.hint: Create a variable like 'testData' that contains an object with properties of different types: strings, numbers, arrays, nested objects, and Date instances.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test object variable is created with multiple data types including primitives, arrays, nested objects, and Date instances.
successCriteria: A test object variable is defined with at least: one primitive value, one array, one nested object, and one Date instance.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
